EventItemActionText:
The Board of Zoning Appeals held its regular meeting at 7:30 p.m. on Wednesday, July 16, 2025, in Town Hall. 

Roll Call: Mr. Dhanjal, Mr. Petersen, Mr. Creed, Mr. Gadell, Mr. Nash, Mr. Rettinger, and Mr. Lowther were present.

 Staff present: Zoning Administrator Andrea West and Board Clerk Yaska Camacho Castillo.

Ms. West presented a variance request for the property located on a cul-de-sac, with an 11,148 square foot lot, built in 1971. The home is in the RS 12.5 zoning district, which requires a minimum lot size of 12,500 square feet, so the lot is slightly undersized. The property has previously received three variances for a screened porch, garage, and deck. However, code changes now allow the garage and deck encroachments without a variance.
The current request seeks a variance from Section 18-218.2, which requires a 35-foot rear yard setback. The proposed addition is a 35-square-foot connection between two existing cantilevered structures at the rear of the home. While the cantilevered structures themselves are compliant, the addition requires a support beam and post, which turns it into a structure that encroaches into the setback, reducing it to 33.7 feet at its narrowest point.
The proposed interior modification will become part of a new kitchen. Lot coverage requirements are still met, and the addition is the only aspect needing a variance. Ms. West concluded by noting that building plans and renderings were submitted by the applicant and are available for review.

Mr. Creed asked whether the two older variances need to be formally extinguished or modified. Ms. West clarified that no action is required. The variances remain on record for historical purposes, but there's no process or need to modify or remove them, since the current code no longer requires them.

The applicant Gregory Stolp -320 Westview Ct. NE was sworn in for his testimony. The applicant thanked the board and reiterated the request for a variance, aligning with the staff summary. He explained that they are renovating their home and plan to connect two existing rear bump-outs to create one continuous structure. This results in a modest 16-inch encroachment into the 35-foot rear yard setback, totaling about 14 square feet.
He emphasized that the change is minimal and does not significantly alter the appearance of the home. The applicant also shared that he spoke with all four adjacent neighbors, three submitted written support, and the fourth verbally expressed no objection. Other cul-de-sac neighbors are aware, though not directly contacted.

Mr. Creed asked for clarification about the variance request, confirming that only the yellow-highlighted area on the diagram, about 14 square feet, encroaching 16 inches into the rear yard setback, is the subject of the variance. The applicant confirmed that this is correct and that it's the only part requiring a variance.
There were no further comments from the board or the public. 

Mr. Gadell made a motion to close the public hearing, and Mr. Creed seconded the motion. 

Mr. Rettinger made a motion to approve the request for a variance from Section 18-218.2. RS-12.5 Dimensional Standards., Rear Yard, of the Town of Vienna Zoning Code, to construct an addition and modify an existing cantilevered structure at the rear of a dwelling located at 320 Westview Ct. NE, in the RS-12.5, Single-Unit Detached Residential zone, resulting in a rear yard setback of 33 feet and 7 inches.

Motion: Mr. Rettinger
Second: Mr. Petersen 
Motion Carried 7-0

The discussion included the following points:

• Mr. Dhanjal expressed appreciation for the letters of support from the neighbors and the applicant’s effort to communicate with them. He noted that the encroachment is minimal (“de minimis”) and was glad to see the applicant has supportive neighbors.

• Mr. Rettinger shared that he previously lived on a cul-de-sac in Vienna and acknowledged that such lots often have irregular shapes, which can present a hardship when expanding a home. He noted this as a relevant factor in considering the variance request.
EventItemTitle: Request for approval of a variance from Section 18-218.2. RS-12.5 Dimensional Standards., Rear Yard, of the Town of Vienna Zoning Code, to construct an addition and modify an existing cantilevered structure at the rear of a dwelling located at 320 Westview Ct. NE, in the RS-12.5, Single-Unit Detached Residential zone.

EventItemActionText:
Ms. West's presentation concerned a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) request for a new business, Clay and Kiln, a pottery studio proposed at 390 B Maple Ave. East, located at the corner of Beulah and Maple Avenue. The property consists of two co-owned parcels, a white corner building, and a row of brick townhouse office condos, with shared parking.

Key points from her presentation are as follows:
• The site is in the AE (Maple Avenue East Gateway) zoning district and designated mixed-use in the Comprehensive Master Plan, allowing for both commercial and some residential use.
• The site has existing parking, though slightly less than what was shown in a 1963 plan. The applicant recently re-striped the lot to better organize the current parking.
• This is the first CUP in this cluster of buildings, prompting staff to review some older site plan issues.
• The business use (pottery studio with a kiln) is permitted under the CUP process.
• The fire department has approved fire safety plans for the kiln.
• Staff believes parking is adequate for current demand, and the request aligns with zoning and the comprehensive plan.
• The board may impose additional conditions on the permit if needed.

Mr. Dhanjal asked about the location and safety of the kiln for the proposed pottery studio. Ms. West explained:
• The kiln is located behind a corrugated steel panel in a covered patio area at the rear of the building (customers enter from the front).
• The applicant cleaned and prepared the area to ensure it was safe for the kiln.
• Fire department approval was obtained before proceeding with the application. Their review included:
o Distances to nearby fire hydrants
o Mitigation plans in case of a fire
• No building or fire suppression permits were triggered, as the interior work was minimal and the kiln is outside.
• If additional requirements were needed, the fire department would have communicated them during the plan review.

Mr. Creed asked whether the kiln is turned off when the building is closed. Ms. West deferred the question, stating that the applicant would be the appropriate person to answer specific operational questions about the kiln. Mr. Creed accepted that response.

Mr. Gadell requested a review of the parking slide and inquired about the occupant of building #392, as well as whether there might be any anticipated parking issues.

Ms. West was unsure and suggested that the applicant might be better able to answer that question. Mr. Gadell agreed to wait and direct the question to the applicant.

Mr. Lowther inquired about the Town's role in managing commercial parking, particularly whether it is responsible for preventing overflow into neighborhoods and protecting parking for other tenants.Ms. West responded that it’s a shared responsibility between the Town and the property owner. 

Key points included:

• The site is older, and its parking does not fully align with current standards.
• Staff worked with the applicant to determine how many spaces could be striped to meet the needs of the proposed use.
• The parking standard for specialized instruction (like pottery classes) is more flexible, based on the number of instructors and participants.
• The applicant stated there would be a maximum of 15 people at a time, mostly adults, which affects parking expectations.
• If the use involved children (as in past cases), more parking or shared parking agreements may have been required.
• This business will not operate at the same time as others on-site, which helps avoid conflicts.
• Staff ultimately considered the existing site conditions when evaluating parking adequacy.

Mr. Creed raised concerns about traffic flow, asking whether vehicles entering Maple Avenue can safely exit by backing out, or if it effectively becomes one-way traffic exiting onto Beulah Road due to the slanted parking configuration. Ms. West was not entirely sure but noted that there appears to be some space between the parking area and Maple Avenue. She said that a sidewalk is present, possibly providing a buffer. She doesn't believe this will be an issue. 

The applicant, Pinar Turhan- 390 B Maple Ave E, was sworn in for her testimony. She shared her vision for opening a pottery studio, which will offer classes and membership programs. Members will also be able to use the space independently. Her goal is to build a creative community centered around a shared love for clay and artistic expression.

Mr. Gadell inquired about the class size. The applicant explained that classes will be limited to 8 people at a time, with no overlapping sessions. Classes are scheduled for either the morning or evening, typically from 10 AM to 1 PM or 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM. The studio is primarily geared toward adults, not children or teens. The maximum occupancy at any given time will be 8 students.

Mr. Petersen asked how many wheels were available. The applicant stated that she currently has 9 pottery wheels, 8 for students and 1 for the instructor, and plans to use one electric kiln initially, due to the high cost of equipment. While she does not plan to expand beyond 9 wheels for now because of space limitations, she hopes to rent a larger space in the future. The applicant also offer two hand-building classes, with one held upstairs, but emphasized that only one class will be in session at a time. The second space will serve as storage or studio use when not in use for classes.

Mr. Creed asked about the kiln firing schedule and whether it would continue operating after business hours. The applicant explained:

• The firing process takes time, with the kiln reaching peak temperature in about 8 hours, followed by a long cooling phase.
• The plan is to operate the kiln during the day while the applicant is present, so the peak heat occurs during business hours, and it cools down afterward while he applicant is not present.
• Evening class students (6–9 PM) will not be firing their pottery immediately, as pieces need to dry for about a month before being fired.
• Firing won’t happen immediately, and high temperatures won’t be present at night when the studio is closed.
• The applicant also noted that security cameras will be installed to ensure safety.

Mr. Nash asked for clarification on the parking and traffic flow. It was confirmed that when entering the site, vehicles will park in the diagonal spots near the end and rear of the building, where most parking is located. After parking, traffic will flow out to Beulah Road, not back onto Maple Avenue. Students will exit via Beulah after classes.

With no further questions from the board or comments from the public, a motion to close the public hearing was in order. 

Mr. Gadell made a motion to close the public hearing, and Mr. Lowther seconded the motion. 

Mr. Dhanjal requested to reopen the public hearing to ask the applicant about Building 392. All board members agreed to reopen the hearing.

Murat Turhan - 394 Maple Ave E – was sworn in to speak. 

Mr. Gadell asked who occupies Building #392 to better understand parking needs. Mr. Turhan clarified that Building 392 is used solely for storage and has no water access, confirming that it is not used for active business operations.

Mr. Creed asked Mr. Turhan how often he needs to access the building for storage. Mr. Turhan stated that he accesses Building 392 for storage only about once a month, as it’s a small space and he has another primary storage area. He does not anticipate any parking conflicts. Additionally, he mentioned having a showroom in Building 394, which operates by phone only, with no daily customer traffic. He confirmed that Building 392 is rarely used and he does not rely on its parking, which is shared with his wife (applicant).

Mr. Gadell made a motion to close the public hearing, and Mr. Dhanjal seconded the motion. 

Mr. Creed made a motion to approve the request for approval of a Conditional Use Permit, per Sec. 18-304., to allow Specialized Instruction for a ceramics studio and classes at 390 B Maple Ave E, for Clay & Kiln Studio LLC, in the AE zone.

Motion: Mr. Creed
Second: Mr. Lowther 
Motion Carried 7-0

Board members expressed strong support for the proposed pottery studio, emphasizing its alignment with the town’s goals for specialized instruction and community enrichment. 

Key points included:
• The location and parking were considered adequate, and the limited hours reduce the chance of conflicts.
• One member noted this is exactly the type of use envisioned when the zoning code was updated.
• Personal anecdotes were shared, highlighting the lasting impact of early exposure to ceramics, with one member's daughter continuing clay work into adulthood, and another’s niece recently taking up pottery.
• Overall, the board saw the project as a positive contribution to the Town of Vienna's arts and community offerings.
EventItemTitle: Request for approval of a Conditional Use Permit, per Sec. 18-304., to allow Specialized Instruction for a ceramics studio and classes at 390 B Maple Ave E, for Clay & Kiln Studio LLC, in the AE zone.

Regular Meeting

1. The minutes of the June 18, 2025, meeting were approved as submitted. Mr. Creed abstained, as he was not present at that meeting.

2. Ms. West stated that there will be at least 3 items on the agenda for the September meeting and that Director David Levy will be covering for her.

The meeting was adjourned at 8:08 pm.

Yaska Camacho Castillo
Clerk to the Board

About the Board of Zoning Appeals

About the Board of Zoning Appeals:

The Board of Zoning Appeals is a quasi-judicial board comprised of seven members – all of whom are residents of the Town of Vienna, VA.  The Board serves as an arm of the Fairfax County Circuit Court, as all members are appointed to the Board by the Court after receipt of recommendation from the Vienna Mayor and Town Council. 

The Board is empowered by the Code of Virginia to:

•Hear and decide appeals from any order, requirement, decision or determination of the Zoning Administrator.
•Grant variances from the Zoning Ordinance – as defined in Section 15.2201 of the Code of Virginia – as will not be contrary to the public interest, when, owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the provisions will unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property to a degree that is not shared generally by other properties within the same zone or district, and its authorization will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent properties or change the character of the neighborhood
•Hear and decide applications for interpretation of the Zoning District Map when there is any uncertainty as to the location of the boundary line.
•Grant Conditional Use Permits in accordance with the provisions of Section 18-209 – 216 of the Vienna Town Code.

The Board of Zoning Appeals does not have the power to change the Zoning Ordinance or the rezone property.  Those powers rest with the Mayor and Town Council.  Please be advised, the Board decides each application on its own merit – there are no precedents.

The Board will first consider each application during the Public Hearing portion of the meeting.  As part of the Virginia Court System, the Board of Zoning Appeals takes sworn testimony and each participant will be sworn in prior to offering comments.  During the public hearing each agenda shall be closed a decision will be rendered. 

The grant of a Conditional Use Permit, Variance, or appeal from a decision by the Town’s Zoning Administrator requires an affirmative vote of no less than a majority of membership, of the Board. The Board consists of 7 members and a majority consists 4 members.  If the applicant is unable to stay for the Board’s decision portion, the applicant may learn the Board’s decision by contacting staff.  

The second portion of the meeting – the Regular Meeting – is for approval of meeting minutes and new business and will convene after the Public Hearing has been closed.  

If any party is not satisfied with the decision of the Board, an appeal may be filed with the Circuit Court of Fairfax County within 30 days after the issuance of the Board’s decision on the matter.
